blurb:
Los Bravos has been around long enough that a lot of people in the area already have it in their rotation. The kitchen is the reason. The food is consistently good and it works for a casual weeknight dinner, a family lunch, or just grabbing something quick when you're in the area.

The food side of things is what keeps people coming back. Long-time regulars swear by it, and with 884 reviews at a 4.2 that's not an accident.

Fair heads up on the drinks though: if you're planning to do margaritas, reviewers who've been going for years have noticed the bar prices have climbed pretty noticeably compared to other spots nearby. Go for the food, just don't be caught off guard when the drink tab comes.

blurb:
My wife and I ended up here on a Saturday afternoon when we needed something casual and filling, and it delivered. The vibe is laid-back and easy, good for lunch with the family or a low-key dinner when you don't want to think too hard about where to go. We brought the kids once and they were perfectly happy, which is always a win.

The menu leans into melts and comfort food, and most people seem to gravitate toward the classic options. Fair warning from the reviews: a couple folks have mentioned things run on the greasier side, so if that's not your thing, maybe go in with that expectation. My son and I noticed it a bit too, but neither of us ruled out going back.

Open every day starting at 11am, so it works for lunch or dinner pretty much any day of the week.

blurb:
I genuinely don't know why it took me this long to walk through the door. JJ's is right there on Roswell Road and I drove past it forever before finally stopping in. Now it's a regular rotation for us on Friday nights when nobody wants to cook.

Get the garlic cheese knots. I'm not being dramatic, they might be the best version of that thing I've had locally. The stuffed pizza is also worth ordering if you've never had it, it's not what you expect but in the best possible way. My wife and I have done the classic pizza too and it's solid all the way through.

One heads up: they're closed on Tuesdays. We learned that the slightly annoying way. Every other day they're open starting at 11am, and Friday and Saturday they go until 10pm.

blurb:
This is the place you go when you want energy. High ceilings, craft beer on tap, a tiki bar out back, and live music on the weekends. It's loud and fun and exactly right for a post-game night out or a Friday where you just want to decompress with friends. Not a quiet date night spot, but for everything else it checks a lot of boxes.

The wings are the main event, and with over 1,900 reviews sitting at a 4.4, people keep coming back. The tap house setup means there are solid beer options to go alongside them. My wife and I have done the outdoor tiki bar on a warm evening and it hits different out there.

Open every day until 11pm, so it also works late when most other spots around here have already called it.

blurb:
This one is a hidden gem and I mean that honestly. It's tucked inside a supermarket on Allgood, so driving past it you'd never think twice. But the taqueria in the back is putting out food that a lot of dedicated Mexican spots can't touch.

The pastor is the move. Reviewers are raving about it and I get why, perfectly seasoned and not overdone. The pupusas are also worth ordering, specifically the beans and cheese. And if you want a full plate, the chicken breast with rice and homemade beans is a solid lunch. My wife would go back for the tortas alone.

Just know Thursdays they close earlier than the rest of the week, so plan around that if you're going for a weeknight dinner.
